items.title: Microsoft quietly purges 32GB of RAM recommendations from its website — company reels from the effects of the memory shortage as it released 8GB base models for Surface laptops this year
items.description: Microsoft once recommended 32GB of RAM as a future-proof "no worries" upgrade for gamers, but it seems that it wants you to forget that it ever gave that suggestion. That's because laptop manufacturers, including Microsoft itself, has once again started selling models with a base configuration of 8GB of RAM as companies memory prices skyrocket out of control.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter In May of this year, Microsoft said that 32GB of RAM is now the future-proof “no worries” configuration if you’re a gaming enthusiast, and that 16GB of RAM is now the new “practical starting point” if you want to have a smooth experience with Windows 11. However, it seems that the company is backtracking on this announcement as it removes all references to the post on the Windows Learning Center website, according to Windows Latest.Microsoft previously posted a blog titled “How to optimize your gaming PC setup” in November 2025, where it said that 32GB is the ideal capacity for hardcore gamers who demand the best possible quality for AAA games or use mods a lot. However, this page is no longer available, and people who attempt to visit the link are automatically redirected to the Learning Center Homepage.Many manufacturers are once again releasing laptops that just have 8GB of RAM. Microsoft is part of this move, as it dropped its budget Surface Go and Surface Laptop Go models and introduced 8GB base versions of its Surface Pro 12, Surface Laptop 13, and Surface Laptop for Business. Thankfully, Redmond is not leaving users who cannot afford expensive RAM out to dry, as it recently promised to optimize the operating system and reduce its footprint by this year.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Even though Windows 11’s minimum specifications just require 4GB, the prevalence of many web-based apps and interfaces on the OS use up a lot of memory on many systems. While using web-based React and WebView2 is easier for developers, they’re not as efficient as apps that are built to run natively on Windows. This wasn’t a problem when memory was cheap and plentiful, as people could just spend a few dollars to upgrade their Windows PCs. However, now that memory modules are expensive and it’s hard to find the best prices for DDR5 and DDR4 kits, developers are going to be forced to optimize their software to use as little memory as possible.This was actually what Windows programmers had to do in the 1980s and 1990s, when every Microsoft engineer had a stopwatch to ensure that their work remained fast, even on the limited hardware of the time. Even the original Task Manager, which was built by the same person who integrated ZIP file support into Windows, was only 80KB big so that it could run smoothly on “potato” hardware.Hopefully, both Microsoft and app developers will rise to the challenge brought about by the memory shortage and make Windows efficient once more. This is especially true as Microsoft is now facing some competition from macOS and Linux (although Windows is, by far, still the most popular operating system today). items.titleZh: 微软悄然从官网移除32GB内存建议——受内存短缺影响，今年发布8GB基础版Surface笔记本
items.descriptionZh:
微软近期在内存配置建议上出现了明显转向。今年5月，微软曾公开表示，对于游戏发烧友而言，32GB内存是面向未来的“无忧之选”，而16GB则是体验Windows 11流畅运行的“实用起点”。然而，据Windows Latest报道，微软似乎已悄然撤回这一立场，删除了Windows学习中心网站上的相关文章。这篇题为《如何优化你的游戏PC设置》的博客发表于2025年11月，当时明确建议硬核玩家在游玩AAA大作或大量使用模组时配备32GB内存。如今，该页面已无法访问，访问者会被自动重定向至学习中心主页。

值得注意的是，在内存价格高企的背景下，多家制造商再度推出仅搭载8GB内存的笔记本电脑，微软也不例外。该公司砍掉了面向预算市场的Surface Go和Surface Laptop Go产品线，转而推出Surface Pro 12、Surface Laptop 13及Surface for Business等8GB起步的机型。但微软并未抛弃预算有限的用户，承诺在年内优化操作系统、压缩系统内存占用空间。

尽管Windows 11的最低硬件要求仅为4GB内存，但系统内大量基于Web的应用程序和界面（如使用React和WebView2构建的应用）会消耗可观的内存资源。这类跨平台方案对开发者而言更便捷，但其运行效率远不及原生Windows应用。过去内存价格低廉时，用户只需花费少量费用即可升级PC，问题并不突出；但如今DDR5和DDR4内存模组价格高企，开发者被迫着手优化软件，尽可能减少内存占用。

这种局面其实让人回想起上世纪80、90年代——当时每一位微软工程师都随身携带秒表，以确保代码在低配硬件上依然保持流畅。就连那位将ZIP文件支持整合进Windows的任务管理器原始作者，也将该工具压缩至仅仅80KB大小，只为让它在“土豆级”硬件上也能顺畅运行。

面对内存短缺带来的挑战，外界期望微软及第三方应用开发者能重新拾起这种精简高效的传统，让Windows系统再度变得轻快。尤其当macOS和Linux正对微软构成竞争压力时，提升系统效率更显重要——尽管目前Windows仍是绝对主流的桌面操作系统。

items.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX will exclusively use Nvidia GPUs 'because they are the best' — says optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 will be launched into space next year
items.description: Elon Musk's SpaceX and xAI will exclusive use Nvidia AI accelerators for training and inference as companies believe Vera Rubin is the best AI compute architecture available today.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Elon Musk on Tuesday said in an X post that SpaceX and xAI will exclusively use Nvidia GPUs because 'they are the best.' He later clarified during SpaceX's earnings call that Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale system's design is above everything else that is available today, which is certainly praise for Nvidia, but not such a good sign for other developers of merchant AI accelerators.SpaceX has committed to using Nvidia GPUs exclusively because they are the bestAugust 4, 2026"Going forward, we have decided to build exclusively on Nvidia, because we think the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture," Elon Musk said during SpaceX's earnings call. "We think it is the best AI computer, and we greatly value our close cooperation and partnership on many levels with Nvidia. We are exclusive to Nvidia. […] We think the design of the NVL72 VR[200] computer is a much better design than, say, having a standard rack style design."Historically, xAI has exclusively used Nvidia's Hopper and, more recently, Blackwell hardware to train multiple generations of Grok. Although AMD has used Grok-1 on its Instinct MI300X accelerators, there has never been a public announcement or credible evidence that xAI has evaluated or used AMD Instinct, or other non-Nvidia accelerators in production. xAI's Colossus supercomputers have been using Nvidia's accelerators for years, so the official exclusivity looks more like a formality that gives a strong testament for Nvidia rather than a decision that was hard to make.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: When it comes to the praise of the cable-less design of compute trays in Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 VR200 rack system, then Musk's admiration of this architecture is understandable, as while expensive, such trays greatly improve serviceability, assembly speed, and reliability by eliminating a large number of manual cable and hose connections that are common sources of installation errors and failures.Interestingly, but Musk's SpaceX plans to deploy Vera Rubin not only in its own and xAI's data centers, but also in space. You may like SpaceX admits it can't find enough chips for orbital AI, requires 'significantly more than are currently available to us' Behind the scenes at Nvidia's Engineering SuperLab Elon Musk's first-gen orbital data center craft spans wider than a Boeing 747 and runs an interchangeable chip payload "With respect to the Starmind AI satellite, which will be essentially an optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 computer, this is not some sort of far future distant thing; we expect to start launching this next year," Musk said. "We think the design of the NVL72 VR[200] computer is a much better design than, say, having a standard rack style design. We expect to actually deploy this on the ground as well as in orbit, because we think it is going to be a radical simplification of the normal NVL72 rack."Deploying an NVL72-scale machine will be by far a more ambitious project than Nvidia has in mind with its Space-1 Vera Rubin Module that is designed to deploy several, perhaps a dozen, of Rubin AI accelerators in space. 36 Vera CPUs and 72 Rubin AI GPUs offer rather formidable performance, though many questions remain about the cooling and reliability of such racks in space.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

items.titleZh: Elon Musk says SpaceX will exclusively use Nvidia GPUs 'because they are the best' — says optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 will be launched into space next year
items.descriptionZh:
埃隆·马斯克近日在X平台上宣布，SpaceX和xAI将独家采用Nvidia GPU，理由是"它们是最好的"。随后，他在SpaceX财报电话会议上进一步澄清，认为Nvidia的Vera Rubin NVL72机架级系统的设计"优于目前市面上所有可用方案"。这一表态无疑是对Nvidia的极大背书，但对其他商用AI加速器开发商而言，显然不是一个好兆头。

回顾历史，xAI一直使用Nvidia的Hopper和Blackwell硬件来训练其多代Grok模型。虽然AMD曾在其Instinct MI300X加速器上运行过Grok-1模型，但从未有公开声明或可靠证据表明xAI在生产环境中评估或使用过AMD Instinct或其他非Nvidia加速器。xAI的Colossus超算多年来一直依赖Nvidia加速器，因此这次"官方独家"更像是对既有事实的正式确认，是对Nvidia的强力印证，而非一个艰难的决策。

马斯克对Vera Rubin NVL72 VR200机架系统的赞赏集中在其无缆化计算托盘设计上。这种托盘虽然成本高昂，但通过消除大量手工布线和软管连接，大幅提升了可维护性、装配速度和可靠性——这些手工连接正是安装错误和故障的常见来源。

最引人注目的是，马斯克透露SpaceX不仅计划在地面和xAI数据中心部署Vera Rubin，还打算将其送入太空。他提到的"Starmind AI卫星"本质上是一台经过优化的Vera Rubin NVL72计算机，预计明年就开始发射。马斯克表示："我们相信NVL72 VR200计算机的设计远优于标准的机架式设计，我们计划在地面和轨道上同时部署，因为我们认为这将是对常规NVL72机架的彻底简化。"

这一计划比Nvidia自身的Space-1 Vera Rubin Module项目要雄心勃勃得多——后者仅打算在太空中部署若干（可能十几个）Rubin AI加速器。而SpaceX的Starmind卫星将搭载36个Vera CPU和72个Rubin AI GPU，性能相当可观。当然，这种规模的机架在太空中的散热和可靠性仍存在诸多待解难题。

从更广的视角看，这一决定意味着马斯克旗下的AI基础设施战略将深度绑定Nvidia的硬件路线图。Vera Rubin NVL72采用的高密度、无缆化设计不仅适用于地面数据中心，其简洁的架构也为太空部署提供了可能。若Starmind计划成行，这将是人类首次在近地轨道运行机架级AI计算系统，可能为太空AI应用开辟全新范式，包括轨道数据处理、自主卫星操作等场景。同时，这也向AI芯片市场传递了一个清晰信号：在高端AI训练与推理领域，Nvidia的架构优势依然难以撼动。

items.title: Frore claims its LiquidJet can drop Nvidia Rubin GPU temperatures by 10°C — can also boost performance by 15% as hyperscalers eye using delidded GPUs in production environments
items.description: As cooling becomes a crucial element for economic efficiency of AI data centers, Frore claims that using is LiquidJet coldplate could increase efficiency of token generation by 15%.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter It is not a secret that proper cooling ensures longevity and enables hardware to demonstrate its full potential. But when it comes to data center AI hardware, proper cooling also means higher sustained performance, which directly translates into money earned by the owner. Frore Systems, a maker of cooling solutions that are made using semiconductor-grade tools, seems to have a perfect idea of how to reduce the temperature of next-generation AI accelerators and increase their performance by 15%.Tom's Hardware Premium Roadmaps (Image credit: Future)High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Roadmap Nvidia Enterprise GPU and CPU RoadmapAI accelerator RoadmapDesktop GPU Roadmap3D NAND RoadmapFrore Systems last week published a white paper which suggests that improvements to the entire cooling stack — from the GPU packaging and thermal interface materials (TIMs) to coldplates and coolant temperatures — can increase token generation per watt by more than 30%. Meanwhile, one of the company's boldest projections based on an analytical thermal model* is that its LiquidJet coldplate technology alone can lower Nvidia Rubin GPU junction temperatures by up to 12°C, which translates into a 10% to 25% improvement in tokens/Watt, while a 10°C reduction could increase token generation by around 15%.Indeed, modern AI accelerators, such as the upcoming Nvidia Rubin, can dissipate up to 2,400 W, and their die temperatures can easily hit 95°C or more. But while 95°C is not necessarily a problem for silicon longevity, leakage current certainly is. Leakage current rises exponentially with temperature, approximately doubling for every 10°C increase in maximum junction temperature, which is when transistor switching itself also becomes less efficient. As a consequence, hotter GPUs require higher voltages to sustain clocks, which eventually forces Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) to reduce clocks to remain within thermal limits, which in turn will reduce performance and token generation.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Frore Systems)This all leads to a simple conclusion: the better the cooling, the higher the performance and token output. Which is generally right. However, cooling is not as simple, as it depends on multiple factors that can be optimized. Furthermore, for AI data centers, cooling itself is no longer a way to preserve CPUs and accelerators from overheating, but really is a way to maximize their performance and token money generation.Nvidia designs its platforms around Tj(max) temperature; it is one of the fundamental design constraints for the GPU, package, and cooling solution. This works like this: You may like Frore shows off LiquidJet Nexus coldplate for Nvidia Vera Rubin, other AI accelerators Nvidia announces liquid cooling system that runs ‘hotter than a hot tub’ Supermicro shows off Vera Rubin NVL72 rack with all-new type of coolant Nvidia specifies a maximum allowable junction temperature (Tj,max limit). This is the temperature the silicon must not exceed during normal operation. The exact value is not always public, but Frore uses 95°C for Rubin in its analysis.The GPU continuously monitors its junction temperature using tens or hundreds of on-die thermal sensors, yet power management monitors the hottest region.DVFS attempts to maximize performance while staying below the thermal and power limits, so if the GPU has thermal headroom, it can sustain higher clocks or lower voltage. If the junction temperature rises, the firmware gradually adjusts voltage and frequency. If necessary, it throttles to prevent exceeding Tj(max).The problem is that GPUs operate under several simultaneous limits, such as thermal limit (Tj,max), package power limit, current limit, and voltage limit. Usually, power is reached before thermal. Meanwhile, modern cooling systems are designed to prevent silicon from reaching Tj(max). So, even if Nvidia's GPU never reaches Tj(max), lowering the operating junction temperature still improves efficiency because transistor leakage decreases as temperature falls. This is where Frore and its cooling systems come into play.According to Frore, leakage power approximately doubles for every 10°C increase in junction temperature, while transistor switching power rises by about 2% over the same temperature range, so lowering operating temperatures is beneficial even when the processor is not thermally throttling.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThermal resistanceAccording to Frore, the maximum GPU junction temperature used by hardware makers is directed by a deceptively simple equation:Tj(max) = Tinlet + Q × Rtotalwhere coolant inlet temperature, GPU power, and total thermal resistance determine how hot the silicon can be. Meanwhile, total thermal resistance depends on three major elements: the GPU package itself, the thermal interface material between the package, and the coldplate design. As each layer adds thermal resistance, it increases die temperature and reduces overall token money generation. That said, thermal resistance is becoming a major problem, according to the paper. What to read next Nvidia details Rubin architectural optimizations for inference Ingenious modder converts countertop ice machine into an RTX 3060 GPU cooler with a beer fridge thermostat Hotspot temperature sensor on Nvidia's Blackwell gaming GPUs is still accessible if you have access to Nvidia's internal MODS tool Frore claims that delidding the Rubin package dramatically lowers thermal resistance (while this is obvious, I must add again that the paper is based on an analytical thermal model*). According to the paper, an unlidded Rubin package can reduce junction temperature by as much as 20°C compared to one with an integrated heatspreader (IHS), which potentially improves tokens/Watt by up to 35%. Of course, there are disadvantages, as delidded GPUs have lower mechanical reliability. We will talk about it later on. In any case, there are cloud system providers that explore the use of delidded Rubin GPUs to boost their token money generation despite all the risks, according to Frore. (Image credit: Frore Systems)Frore's own contribution is, of course, its coldplate. Conventional coldplates are typically manufactured using skiving, a machining process that creates long, straight microchannels inside a copper block. Frore instead borrows manufacturing techniques from semiconductor fabrication — etching and bonding — to build intricate three-dimensional copper microstructures that address hotspots on the accelerator's silicon. These unique microstructures cannot be produced using traditional machining, at least not cost-efficiently, according to Frore. (Image credit: Frore Systems)Improving efficiencyThe LiquidJet design features short microchannels that are etched around hot spots, multiple cooling stages, and flow routing optimized for the GPU's power-density map. According to the company's analysis, this enables a 6°C to 12°C reduction in junction temperature and improves tokens/Watt by 10% to 25% in the case of the Nvidia Rubin GPU*. A roughly 10°C temperature reduction would therefore correspond to about a 15% increase in token generation efficiency, the paper claims. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Frore Systems) (Image credit: Frore Systems) (Image credit: Frore Systems) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Frore argues that improved coldplate efficiency changes the economics of facility cooling, which is obviously the most important part of the hyperscalers' consideration. Nvidia designed Rubin to operate with coolant entering at up to 45°C, which enables many AI data centers to rely entirely on 'free' cooling without mechanical chillers. While lowering the inlet temperature can further improve GPU efficiency, doing so only makes economic sense if the energy consumed by the chillers is offset by the resulting increase in money token generation. Meanwhile, because LiquidJet requires a lower coolant flow rate to maintain the same junction temperature, it also reduces the chiller coefficient of performance (COP) required for additional cooling to become worthwhile. (Image credit: Frore Systems)In Frore's example, a Rubin GPU equipped with a conventional skived coldplate requires a chiller COP of approximately 6.7 before colder coolant delivers a net efficiency benefit, whereas LiquidJet lowers the break-even COP to around 4.1, which makes mechanical chilling economically attractive across various deployments.One interesting thing about Frore's analysis is that its LiquidJet is more efficient on Rubin data center GPUs compared to Blackwell data center GPUs* due to the higher transistor density of the former.Frore's analysis does not stop at exploring the advantages of its own cooling systems, so the company's analytical thermal model extends to other means by which improved cooling and/or lowered thermal resistance can affect temperatures and therefore money token generation. (Image credit: Frore Systems)One of the most striking claims by Frore concerns Nvidia's upcoming Rubin is that Frore claims that delidding the GPU package — removing the IHS and the graphene TIM placed between the die and the lid — dramatically lowers thermal resistance, which therefore reduces junction temperature by as much as 20°C compared to regular GPUs with IHS, which therefore improves tokens per Watt by up to 35%, according to the model used by Frore.Meanwhile, mechanical reliability becomes a major concern for delidded GPUs. Without the IHS, the bare Rubin GPU packaged using TSMC's CoWoS-L technology becomes considerably more vulnerable to cracking of bridges that connect the two Rubin dies. In fact, even in the Hopper era, some GPUs literally cracked with certain liquid coolers. Furthermore, maintaining uniform contact pressure across multiple exposed dies is substantially more difficult than in the case of monolithic processors. Nonetheless, there are hyperscalers that are exploring the use of delidded Rubin GPUs to increase their token generation and money output.Thermal interface materials play an equally important role. By default, Nvidia's Rubin reportedly addresses the thermal penalty of a lidded package by using liquid indium metal TIM with gold-plated contact surfaces. Frore argues that an unlidded package paired with a high-performance phase-change material such as PTM7950 still exhibits lower overall thermal resistance than a lidded package using liquid metal, which turns into as much as a 14°C junction-temperature advantage and up to a 28% increase in money tokens/Watt, according to Frore's model.SummaryThe key point of Frore's white paper is that cooling has become a key determinant of AI data center profitability, as lower GPU junction temperatures improve token generation efficiency rather than 'just' preventing overheating.In a white paper based on an analytical thermal model, the company claims that its LiquidJet coldplate can lower Nvidia Rubin junction temperatures by 6°C to 12°C and increase tokens/Watt by 10% to 25%, while a 10°C reduction could boost token generation by about 15%.In addition, the company argues that more efficient coldplates make mechanical chilling economically viable across a wider range of AI data centers as it lowers the break-even chiller efficiency required to offset cooling power consumption.Finally, Frore claims that delidding Rubin and optimizing thermal interface materials can reduce thermal resistance further and improve tokens/Watt by up to 35%, albeit at the cost of greater mechanical risk for these accelerators.*It should be noted that Frore's analysis is based on an analytical thermal model rather than experimental results. The paper builds on the thermal resistance equation (Tj = Tinlet + Q × Rtotal), published or assumed operating parameters for Nvidia's Rubin GPU, and the company's own estimates of how different coldplate designs affect thermal resistance. items.titleZh: Frore claims its LiquidJet can drop Nvidia Rubin GPU temperatures by 10°C — can also boost performance by 15% as hyperscalers eye using delidded GPUs in production environments
items.descriptionZh:
在AI数据中心领域，散热已不再是单纯的防止硬件过热问题，而是直接决定AI加速器性能输出和盈利能力的关键因素。Frore Systems是一家采用半导体级制造工具生产冷却方案的厂商，其最新发布的白皮书指出，通过优化从GPU封装、导热界面材料（TIM）到冷板、冷却液温度的整个冷却链条，可将token生成效率（tokens/Watt）提升超过30%。这一论断揭示了冷却技术在现代AI基础设施中扮演的战略性角色。

**温度与性能的深层物理关联**  
现代AI加速器（如即将问世的Nvidia Rubin）功耗高达2400W，芯片结温可轻松突破95°C。虽然95°C本身不直接损害硅片寿命，但漏电流会随温度指数级增长——结温每升高10°C，漏电流近似翻倍，同时晶体管开关效率下降。为维持时钟频率，GPU需要更高的电压，进而触发动态电压频率调整（DVFS）机制降频，最终导致性能下滑和token产出减少。因此，更优的冷却直接意味着更高的性能和经济效益。

**热阻公式：冷却设计的核心约束**  
Frore的分析基于一个简洁的公式：Tj(max) = T入口 + Q × R总（最大结温 = 冷却液入口温度 + 芯片功耗 × 总热阻）。总热阻由三个主要环节构成：GPU封装本身、封装与冷板之间的导热界面材料（TIM）、冷板设计。每一层热阻都会抬高芯片温度，降低token产出。Nvidia在设计平台时，会为GPU指定最大允许结温（如95°C），而实际运行中，即使未触及该阈值，降低工作温度也能通过减少漏电流来提升效率。

**LiquidJet冷板：半导体工艺的跨界创新**  
传统冷板多采用“刮削”（skiving）工艺制造，在铜块中形成长直微通道。Frore则借鉴半导体制造的蚀刻与键合技术，构建出复杂的三维铜微结构，能够精准针对AI芯片上的热点区域进行冷却。其设计特点包括：围绕热点蚀刻短微通道、多级冷却阶段、以及根据GPU功率密度地图优化的流道布局。根据其分析模型，该技术在Nvidia Rubin GPU上可实现6°C至12°C的结温降低，对应tokens/Watt提升10%至25%，约10°C的降温可带来约15%的token生成效率提升。

**封装层面革新：去盖与导热材料的潜力**  
Frore的白皮书进一步探讨了封装层面的优化空间。其最大胆的预测是：移除Rubin GPU的集成散热器（IHS）和其中的石墨烯TIM，即“去盖”（delidding），可将封装热阻大幅降低，使结温比常规带盖封装低多达20°C，从而提升tokens/Watt多达35%。值得注意的是，已有一些云服务提供商正在探索使用去盖Rubin GPU以提升盈利能力。不过，去盖后芯片的机械可靠性成为重大隐患——裸片在安装和运行中更易因压力不均而开裂，尤其是Rubin采用TSMC CoWoS-L技术连接两颗芯片，互连桥的脆弱性更高。

**导热界面材料的优化对比**  
导热界面材料同样影响显著。据称Nvidia Rubin在带盖封装中默认使用液态金属铟TIM和镀金接触面。而Frore的方案是：去盖封装搭配高性能相变材料（如PTM7950），其整体热阻仍然低于采用液态金属的带盖封装，可带来多达14°C的结温优势和高达28%的tokens/Watt提升。

**设施冷却的经济性变革**  
更高效的冷板不仅影响芯片本身，还改变了数据中心设施冷却的经济模型。Nvidia Rubin设计支持最高45°C的冷却液入口温度，使许多AI数据中心能完全依赖“免费”的室外冷源，无需机械制冷机。虽然进一步降低入口温度能提升GPU效率，但必须权衡制冷机能耗与token收益。Frore的LiquidJet冷板因在相同结温下需要更低的冷却液流量，降低了机械制冷变得划算所需的制冷机能效比（COP）盈亏平衡点。具体而言，传统冷板需要COP约6.7才能从更冷冷却液中获利，而LiquidJet将这一阈值降至约4.1，使机械制冷在多种部署场景下更具经济吸引力。

**技术对比与适用范围**  
Frore的分析还指出，由于Rubin数据中心的晶体管密度高于Blackwell，LiquidJet冷板在Rubin上的效率提升更为显著。

**总结与重要提示**  
Frore白皮书的核心观点是：冷却已成为AI数据中心盈利能力的决定性变量——降低GPU结温不只是防止过热，而是直接提升token生成效率。基于分析热模型（非实验数据），该公司声称其LiquidJet冷板可降低结温6-12°C、提升tokens/Watt 10-25%；更高效的冷板可使机械制冷在更广泛的数据中心中具备经济性；而去盖封装和优化TIM可进一步降低热阻、提升tokens/Watt达35%，但伴随机械可靠性风险。需要强调的是，这些结论均基于Frore自己的分析模型，实际效果有待真实环境验证。

items.content: Driven by demand for AI capacity, AMD’s data center revenue more than doubled year-over-year in its latest earnings report, reaching $6.7 billion. That’s up from $5.8 billion in Q1, and jumping 107 percent from the $3.2 billion it reported for the same period a year ago. During Tuesday’s earnings call, AMD CEO Lisa Su said the company expects “data center segment revenue to more than double year-over-year in 2027,” as well.At the same time, AMD’s gaming revenue fell 31 percent compared to last year, to $779 million, as price hikes and component shortages slowed sales for the Xbox Series X / S, PS5, and Valve’s Steam Deck. On a call after the earnings were released, Su told analysts that, “Gaming graphics revenue also declined year-over-year, as higher industry-wide component costs contributed to higher graphics card prices and weighed on overall demand.”Image: AMD“Revenue increased 50 percent year-over-year to a record $11.5 billion, driven by continued strength in our Data Center business, which represented 58% of company revenue in the quarter,” wrote AMD CFO Jean Hu. Its overall PC and gaming business revenue grew six percent compared to last year, with Client revenue up 23 percent thanks to Ryzen processor sales.“AI is driving a significant expansion in demand for compute across all of our markets, and our leadership portfolio and growing customer visibility position us exceptionally well to capture this expanding opportunity and deliver substantial revenue and earnings growth in the years ahead,” said AMD CEO Lisa Su.Update, August 4th: Added comments from AMD’s earnings call.

items.titleZh: AMD数据中心业务蓬勃发展，游戏业务退居其次
items.descriptionZh:
AMD最新季度财报显示，在AI算力需求爆发的强力驱动下，其数据中心业务表现极为亮眼：该部门营收达到67亿美元，较上季度的58亿美元环比增长，更同比暴增107%（去年同期为32亿美元）。这一数字意味着数据中心已经取代传统PC成为AMD的绝对增长引擎，当季占公司总营收的58%。AMD CEO苏姿丰在财报电话会上进一步表示，预计2027年数据中心部门营收仍将保持同比翻倍以上的增长势头，彰显出市场对AI加速芯片持续且旺盛的渴求。

与此形成鲜明对比的是，AMD的游戏业务遭遇明显滑铁卢，季度营收降至7.79亿美元，同比下降31%。苏姿丰将下滑归因于行业性组件成本上涨推高了显卡价格，从而抑制了消费需求；Xbox Series X/S、PS5以及Steam Deck等游戏主机的销售也因价格因素和元器件短缺而承压。这凸显出AI算力对芯片产能的挤占正在深刻重塑半导体行业的供需格局，游戏显卡优先级被迫后移。

从整体财务数据看，AMD当季总营收创下115亿美元的历史纪录，同比增长50%。CFO Jean Hu在报告中强调，增长主要源于数据中心的持续强力表现。分业务来看，客户端（PC）业务营收同比增长23%，得益于锐龙（Ryzen）处理器出货强劲；PC和游戏业务合计营收同比增长6%，但增长贡献明显由PC端拉动。

在技术层面，AMD目前正通过Instinct系列加速器（如MI300系列）与EPYC服务器处理器双线并进，争夺NVIDIA在AI训练和推理市场的份额。其创新点在于将CPU与GPU（以及HBM高带宽内存）通过Chiplet架构和统一内存池进行异构集成，有效降低数据搬运开销、提升能效比，并借助开放软件生态（ROCm）为用户提供更灵活的AI基础设施选择。苏姿丰强调，“AI正推动所有市场对计算需求的显著扩展”，AMD凭借领先的产品组合和不断增长的客户可见度，有望在未来的算力浪潮中持续实现营收与利润的高速增长。

此次财报背后折射出的行业趋势值得关注：一方面，AI数据中心建设仍处于超级周期，头部云厂商和企业的资本开支持续向加速计算倾斜；另一方面，消费级游戏市场则因芯片产能分流和终端价格上涨而阶段性承压。AMD的战略重心正在全面转向AI基础设施，这一转型既反映了市场结构的深刻变化，也为其在2027年“数据中心营收再翻倍”的远期目标奠定了路径基础。随着更多AI推理负载下沉到企业端和边缘侧，AMD凭借相对开放的生态和更具竞争力的性价比，有望在NVIDIA主导的AI芯片市场中分得更大的蛋糕。

history.title: Microsoft quietly purges 32GB of RAM recommendations from its website — company reels from the effects of the memory shortage as it released 8GB base models for Surface laptops this year
history.description: Microsoft once recommended 32GB of RAM as a future-proof "no worries" upgrade for gamers, but it seems that it wants you to forget that it ever gave that suggestion. That's because laptop manufacturers, including Microsoft itself, has once again started selling models with a base configuration of 8GB of RAM as companies memory prices skyrocket out of control.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter In May of this year, Microsoft said that 32GB of RAM is now the future-proof “no worries” configuration if you’re a gaming enthusiast, and that 16GB of RAM is now the new “practical starting point” if you want to have a smooth experience with Windows 11. However, it seems that the company is backtracking on this announcement as it removes all references to the post on the Windows Learning Center website, according to Windows Latest.Microsoft previously posted a blog titled “How to optimize your gaming PC setup” in November 2025, where it said that 32GB is the ideal capacity for hardcore gamers who demand the best possible quality for AAA games or use mods a lot. However, this page is no longer available, and people who attempt to visit the link are automatically redirected to the Learning Center Homepage.Many manufacturers are once again releasing laptops that just have 8GB of RAM. Microsoft is part of this move, as it dropped its budget Surface Go and Surface Laptop Go models and introduced 8GB base versions of its Surface Pro 12, Surface Laptop 13, and Surface Laptop for Business. Thankfully, Redmond is not leaving users who cannot afford expensive RAM out to dry, as it recently promised to optimize the operating system and reduce its footprint by this year.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Even though Windows 11’s minimum specifications just require 4GB, the prevalence of many web-based apps and interfaces on the OS use up a lot of memory on many systems. While using web-based React and WebView2 is easier for developers, they’re not as efficient as apps that are built to run natively on Windows. This wasn’t a problem when memory was cheap and plentiful, as people could just spend a few dollars to upgrade their Windows PCs. However, now that memory modules are expensive and it’s hard to find the best prices for DDR5 and DDR4 kits, developers are going to be forced to optimize their software to use as little memory as possible.This was actually what Windows programmers had to do in the 1980s and 1990s, when every Microsoft engineer had a stopwatch to ensure that their work remained fast, even on the limited hardware of the time. Even the original Task Manager, which was built by the same person who integrated ZIP file support into Windows, was only 80KB big so that it could run smoothly on “potato” hardware.Hopefully, both Microsoft and app developers will rise to the challenge brought about by the memory shortage and make Windows efficient once more. This is especially true as Microsoft is now facing some competition from macOS and Linux (although Windows is, by far, still the most popular operating system today). history.titleZh: 微软悄然从官网移除32GB内存建议——受内存短缺影响，今年发布8GB基础版Surface笔记本
history.descriptionZh:
微软近期在内存配置建议上出现了明显转向。今年5月，微软曾公开表示，对于游戏发烧友而言，32GB内存是面向未来的“无忧之选”，而16GB则是体验Windows 11流畅运行的“实用起点”。然而，据Windows Latest报道，微软似乎已悄然撤回这一立场，删除了Windows学习中心网站上的相关文章。这篇题为《如何优化你的游戏PC设置》的博客发表于2025年11月，当时明确建议硬核玩家在游玩AAA大作或大量使用模组时配备32GB内存。如今，该页面已无法访问，访问者会被自动重定向至学习中心主页。

值得注意的是，在内存价格高企的背景下，多家制造商再度推出仅搭载8GB内存的笔记本电脑，微软也不例外。该公司砍掉了面向预算市场的Surface Go和Surface Laptop Go产品线，转而推出Surface Pro 12、Surface Laptop 13及Surface for Business等8GB起步的机型。但微软并未抛弃预算有限的用户，承诺在年内优化操作系统、压缩系统内存占用空间。

尽管Windows 11的最低硬件要求仅为4GB内存，但系统内大量基于Web的应用程序和界面（如使用React和WebView2构建的应用）会消耗可观的内存资源。这类跨平台方案对开发者而言更便捷，但其运行效率远不及原生Windows应用。过去内存价格低廉时，用户只需花费少量费用即可升级PC，问题并不突出；但如今DDR5和DDR4内存模组价格高企，开发者被迫着手优化软件，尽可能减少内存占用。

这种局面其实让人回想起上世纪80、90年代——当时每一位微软工程师都随身携带秒表，以确保代码在低配硬件上依然保持流畅。就连那位将ZIP文件支持整合进Windows的任务管理器原始作者，也将该工具压缩至仅仅80KB大小，只为让它在“土豆级”硬件上也能顺畅运行。

面对内存短缺带来的挑战，外界期望微软及第三方应用开发者能重新拾起这种精简高效的传统，让Windows系统再度变得轻快。尤其当macOS和Linux正对微软构成竞争压力时，提升系统效率更显重要——尽管目前Windows仍是绝对主流的桌面操作系统。

history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Elon Musk on Tuesday said in an X post that SpaceX and xAI will exclusively use Nvidia GPUs because 'they are the best.' He later clarified during SpaceX's earnings call that Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale system's design is above everything else that is available today, which is certainly praise for Nvidia, but not such a good sign for other developers of merchant AI accelerators.SpaceX has committed to using Nvidia GPUs exclusively because they are the bestAugust 4, 2026"Going forward, we have decided to build exclusively on Nvidia, because we think the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture," Elon Musk said during SpaceX's earnings call. "We think it is the best AI computer, and we greatly value our close cooperation and partnership on many levels with Nvidia. We are exclusive to Nvidia. […] We think the design of the NVL72 VR[200] computer is a much better design than, say, having a standard rack style design."Historically, xAI has exclusively used Nvidia's Hopper and, more recently, Blackwell hardware to train multiple generations of Grok. Although AMD has used Grok-1 on its Instinct MI300X accelerators, there has never been a public announcement or credible evidence that xAI has evaluated or used AMD Instinct, or other non-Nvidia accelerators in production. xAI's Colossus supercomputers have been using Nvidia's accelerators for years, so the official exclusivity looks more like a formality that gives a strong testament for Nvidia rather than a decision that was hard to make.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: When it comes to the praise of the cable-less design of compute trays in Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 VR200 rack system, then Musk's admiration of this architecture is understandable, as while expensive, such trays greatly improve serviceability, assembly speed, and reliability by eliminating a large number of manual cable and hose connections that are common sources of installation errors and failures.Interestingly, but Musk's SpaceX plans to deploy Vera Rubin not only in its own and xAI's data centers, but also in space. You may like SpaceX admits it can't find enough chips for orbital AI, requires 'significantly more than are currently available to us' Behind the scenes at Nvidia's Engineering SuperLab Elon Musk's first-gen orbital data center craft spans wider than a Boeing 747 and runs an interchangeable chip payload "With respect to the Starmind AI satellite, which will be essentially an optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 computer, this is not some sort of far future distant thing; we expect to start launching this next year," Musk said. We expect to actually deploy this on the ground as well as in orbit, because we think it is going to be a radical simplification of the normal NVL72 rack."Deploying an NVL72-scale machine will be by far a more ambitious project than Nvidia has in mind with its Space-1 Vera Rubin Module that is designed to deploy several, perhaps a dozen, of Rubin AI accelerators in space. 36 Vera CPUs and 72 Rubin AI GPUs offer rather formidable performance, though many questions remain about the cooling and reliability of such racks in space.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

history.titleZh: Elon Musk says SpaceX will exclusively use Nvidia GPUs 'because they are the best' — says optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 will be launched into space next year
history.descriptionZh:
埃隆·马斯克近日在X平台上宣布，SpaceX和xAI将独家采用Nvidia GPU，理由是"它们是最好的"。随后，他在SpaceX财报电话会议上进一步澄清，认为Nvidia的Vera Rubin NVL72机架级系统的设计"优于目前市面上所有可用方案"。这一表态无疑是对Nvidia的极大背书，但对其他商用AI加速器开发商而言，显然不是一个好兆头。

回顾历史，xAI一直使用Nvidia的Hopper和Blackwell硬件来训练其多代Grok模型。虽然AMD曾在其Instinct MI300X加速器上运行过Grok-1模型，但从未有公开声明或可靠证据表明xAI在生产环境中评估或使用过AMD Instinct或其他非Nvidia加速器。xAI的Colossus超算多年来一直依赖Nvidia加速器，因此这次"官方独家"更像是对既有事实的正式确认，是对Nvidia的强力印证，而非一个艰难的决策。

马斯克对Vera Rubin NVL72 VR200机架系统的赞赏集中在其无缆化计算托盘设计上。这种托盘虽然成本高昂，但通过消除大量手工布线和软管连接，大幅提升了可维护性、装配速度和可靠性——这些手工连接正是安装错误和故障的常见来源。

最引人注目的是，马斯克透露SpaceX不仅计划在地面和xAI数据中心部署Vera Rubin，还打算将其送入太空。他提到的"Starmind AI卫星"本质上是一台经过优化的Vera Rubin NVL72计算机，预计明年就开始发射。马斯克表示："我们相信NVL72 VR200计算机的设计远优于标准的机架式设计，我们计划在地面和轨道上同时部署，因为我们认为这将是对常规NVL72机架的彻底简化。"

这一计划比Nvidia自身的Space-1 Vera Rubin Module项目要雄心勃勃得多——后者仅打算在太空中部署若干（可能十几个）Rubin AI加速器。而SpaceX的Starmind卫星将搭载36个Vera CPU和72个Rubin AI GPU，性能相当可观。当然，这种规模的机架在太空中的散热和可靠性仍存在诸多待解难题。

从更广的视角看，这一决定意味着马斯克旗下的AI基础设施战略将深度绑定Nvidia的硬件路线图。Vera Rubin NVL72采用的高密度、无缆化设计不仅适用于地面数据中心，其简洁的架构也为太空部署提供了可能。若Starmind计划成行，这将是人类首次在近地轨道运行机架级AI计算系统，可能为太空AI应用开辟全新范式，包括轨道数据处理、自主卫星操作等场景。同时，这也向AI芯片市场传递了一个清晰信号：在高端AI训练与推理领域，Nvidia的架构优势依然难以撼动。

history.title: Frore claims its LiquidJet can drop Nvidia Rubin GPU temperatures by 10°C — can also boost performance by 15% as hyperscalers eye using delidded GPUs in production environments
history.description: As cooling becomes a crucial element for economic efficiency of AI data centers, Frore claims that using is LiquidJet coldplate could increase efficiency of token generation by 15%.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter It is not a secret that proper cooling ensures longevity and enables hardware to demonstrate its full potential. But when it comes to data center AI hardware, proper cooling also means higher sustained performance, which directly translates into money earned by the owner. Frore Systems, a maker of cooling solutions that are made using semiconductor-grade tools, seems to have a perfect idea of how to reduce the temperature of next-generation AI accelerators and increase their performance by 15%.Tom's Hardware Premium Roadmaps (Image credit: Future)High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Roadmap Nvidia Enterprise GPU and CPU RoadmapAI accelerator RoadmapDesktop GPU Roadmap3D NAND RoadmapFrore Systems last week published a white paper which suggests that improvements to the entire cooling stack — from the GPU packaging and thermal interface materials (TIMs) to coldplates and coolant temperatures — can increase token generation per watt by more than 30%. Meanwhile, one of the company's boldest projections based on an analytical thermal model* is that its LiquidJet coldplate technology alone can lower Nvidia Rubin GPU junction temperatures by up to 12°C, which translates into a 10% to 25% improvement in tokens/Watt, while a 10°C reduction could increase token generation by around 15%.Indeed, modern AI accelerators, such as the upcoming Nvidia Rubin, can dissipate up to 2,400 W, and their die temperatures can easily hit 95°C or more. But while 95°C is not necessarily a problem for silicon longevity, leakage current certainly is. Leakage current rises exponentially with temperature, approximately doubling for every 10°C increase in maximum junction temperature, which is when transistor switching itself also becomes less efficient. As a consequence, hotter GPUs require higher voltages to sustain clocks, which eventually forces Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) to reduce clocks to remain within thermal limits, which in turn will reduce performance and token generation.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Frore Systems)This all leads to a simple conclusion: the better the cooling, the higher the performance and token output. Which is generally right. However, cooling is not as simple, as it depends on multiple factors that can be optimized. Furthermore, for AI data centers, cooling itself is no longer a way to preserve CPUs and accelerators from overheating, but really is a way to maximize their performance and token money generation.Nvidia designs its platforms around Tj(max) temperature; it is one of the fundamental design constraints for the GPU, package, and cooling solution. This works like this: You may like Frore shows off LiquidJet Nexus coldplate for Nvidia Vera Rubin, other AI accelerators Nvidia announces liquid cooling system that runs ‘hotter than a hot tub’ Supermicro shows off Vera Rubin NVL72 rack with all-new type of coolant Nvidia specifies a maximum allowable junction temperature (Tj,max limit). This is the temperature the silicon must not exceed during normal operation. The exact value is not always public, but Frore uses 95°C for Rubin in its analysis.The GPU continuously monitors its junction temperature using tens or hundreds of on-die thermal sensors, yet power management monitors the hottest region.DVFS attempts to maximize performance while staying below the thermal and power limits, so if the GPU has thermal headroom, it can sustain higher clocks or lower voltage. If the junction temperature rises, the firmware gradually adjusts voltage and frequency. If necessary, it throttles to prevent exceeding Tj(max).The problem is that GPUs operate under several simultaneous limits, such as thermal limit (Tj,max), package power limit, current limit, and voltage limit. Usually, power is reached before thermal. Meanwhile, modern cooling systems are designed to prevent silicon from reaching Tj(max). So, even if Nvidia's GPU never reaches Tj(max), lowering the operating junction temperature still improves efficiency because transistor leakage decreases as temperature falls. This is where Frore and its cooling systems come into play.According to Frore, leakage power approximately doubles for every 10°C increase in junction temperature, while transistor switching power rises by about 2% over the same temperature range, so lowering operating temperatures is beneficial even when the processor is not thermally throttling.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThermal resistanceAccording to Frore, the maximum GPU junction temperature used by hardware makers is directed by a deceptively simple equation:Tj(max) = Tinlet + Q × Rtotalwhere coolant inlet temperature, GPU power, and total thermal resistance determine how hot the silicon can be. Meanwhile, total thermal resistance depends on three major elements: the GPU package itself, the thermal interface material between the package, and the coldplate design. As each layer adds thermal resistance, it increases die temperature and reduces overall token money generation. That said, thermal resistance is becoming a major problem, according to the paper. What to read next Nvidia details Rubin architectural optimizations for inference Ingenious modder converts countertop ice machine into an RTX 3060 GPU cooler with a beer fridge thermostat Hotspot temperature sensor on Nvidia's Blackwell gaming GPUs is still accessible if you have access to Nvidia's internal MODS tool Frore claims that delidding the Rubin package dramatically lowers thermal resistance (while this is obvious, I must add again that the paper is based on an analytical thermal model*). According to the paper, an unlidded Rubin package can reduce junction temperature by as much as 20°C compared to one with an integrated heatspreader (IHS), which potentially improves tokens/Watt by up to 35%. Of course, there are disadvantages, as delidded GPUs have lower mechanical reliability. We will talk about it later on. In any case, there are cloud system providers that explore the use of delidded Rubin GPUs to boost their token money generation despite all the risks, according to Frore. (Image credit: Frore Systems)Frore's own contribution is, of course, its coldplate. Conventional coldplates are typically manufactured using skiving, a machining process that creates long, straight microchannels inside a copper block. Frore instead borrows manufacturing techniques from semiconductor fabrication — etching and bonding — to build intricate three-dimensional copper microstructures that address hotspots on the accelerator's silicon. These unique microstructures cannot be produced using traditional machining, at least not cost-efficiently, according to Frore. (Image credit: Frore Systems)Improving efficiencyThe LiquidJet design features short microchannels that are etched around hot spots, multiple cooling stages, and flow routing optimized for the GPU's power-density map. According to the company's analysis, this enables a 6°C to 12°C reduction in junction temperature and improves tokens/Watt by 10% to 25% in the case of the Nvidia Rubin GPU*. A roughly 10°C temperature reduction would therefore correspond to about a 15% increase in token generation efficiency, the paper claims. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Frore Systems) (Image credit: Frore Systems) (Image credit: Frore Systems) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Frore argues that improved coldplate efficiency changes the economics of facility cooling, which is obviously the most important part of the hyperscalers' consideration. Nvidia designed Rubin to operate with coolant entering at up to 45°C, which enables many AI data centers to rely entirely on 'free' cooling without mechanical chillers. While lowering the inlet temperature can further improve GPU efficiency, doing so only makes economic sense if the energy consumed by the chillers is offset by the resulting increase in money token generation. Meanwhile, because LiquidJet requires a lower coolant flow rate to maintain the same junction temperature, it also reduces the chiller coefficient of performance (COP) required for additional cooling to become worthwhile. (Image credit: Frore Systems)In Frore's example, a Rubin GPU equipped with a conventional skived coldplate requires a chiller COP of approximately 6.7 before colder coolant delivers a net efficiency benefit, whereas LiquidJet lowers the break-even COP to around 4.1, which makes mechanical chilling economically attractive across various deployments.One interesting thing about Frore's analysis is that its LiquidJet is more efficient on Rubin data center GPUs compared to Blackwell data center GPUs* due to the higher transistor density of the former.Frore's analysis does not stop at exploring the advantages of its own cooling systems, so the company's analytical thermal model extends to other means by which improved cooling and/or lowered thermal resistance can affect temperatures and therefore money token generation. (Image credit: Frore Systems)One of the most striking claims by Frore concerns Nvidia's upcoming Rubin is that Frore claims that delidding the GPU package — removing the IHS and the graphene TIM placed between the die and the lid — dramatically lowers thermal resistance, which therefore reduces junction temperature by as much as 20°C compared to regular GPUs with IHS, which therefore improves tokens per Watt by up to 35%, according to the model used by Frore.Meanwhile, mechanical reliability becomes a major concern for delidded GPUs. Without the IHS, the bare Rubin GPU packaged using TSMC's CoWoS-L technology becomes considerably more vulnerable to cracking of bridges that connect the two Rubin dies. In fact, even in the Hopper era, some GPUs literally cracked with certain liquid coolers. Furthermore, maintaining uniform contact pressure across multiple exposed dies is substantially more difficult than in the case of monolithic processors. Nonetheless, there are hyperscalers that are exploring the use of delidded Rubin GPUs to increase their token generation and money output.Thermal interface materials play an equally important role. By default, Nvidia's Rubin reportedly addresses the thermal penalty of a lidded package by using liquid indium metal TIM with gold-plated contact surfaces. Frore argues that an unlidded package paired with a high-performance phase-change material such as PTM7950 still exhibits lower overall thermal resistance than a lidded package using liquid metal, which turns into as much as a 14°C junction-temperature advantage and up to a 28% increase in money tokens/Watt, according to Frore's model.SummaryThe key point of Frore's white paper is that cooling has become a key determinant of AI data center profitability, as lower GPU junction temperatures improve token generation efficiency rather than 'just' preventing overheating.In a white paper based on an analytical thermal model, the company claims that its LiquidJet coldplate can lower Nvidia Rubin junction temperatures by 6°C to 12°C and increase tokens/Watt by 10% to 25%, while a 10°C reduction could boost token generation by about 15%.In addition, the company argues that more efficient coldplates make mechanical chilling economically viable across a wider range of AI data centers as it lowers the break-even chiller efficiency required to offset cooling power consumption.Finally, Frore claims that delidding Rubin and optimizing thermal interface materials can reduce thermal resistance further and improve tokens/Watt by up to 35%, albeit at the cost of greater mechanical risk for these accelerators.*It should be noted that Frore's analysis is based on an analytical thermal model rather than experimental results. The paper builds on the thermal resistance equation (Tj = Tinlet + Q × Rtotal), published or assumed operating parameters for Nvidia's Rubin GPU, and the company's own estimates of how different coldplate designs affect thermal resistance. history.titleZh: Frore claims its LiquidJet can drop Nvidia Rubin GPU temperatures by 10°C — can also boost performance by 15% as hyperscalers eye using delidded GPUs in production environments
history.descriptionZh:
在AI数据中心领域，散热已不再是单纯的防止硬件过热问题，而是直接决定AI加速器性能输出和盈利能力的关键因素。Frore Systems是一家采用半导体级制造工具生产冷却方案的厂商，其最新发布的白皮书指出，通过优化从GPU封装、导热界面材料（TIM）到冷板、冷却液温度的整个冷却链条，可将token生成效率（tokens/Watt）提升超过30%。这一论断揭示了冷却技术在现代AI基础设施中扮演的战略性角色。

**温度与性能的深层物理关联**  
现代AI加速器（如即将问世的Nvidia Rubin）功耗高达2400W，芯片结温可轻松突破95°C。虽然95°C本身不直接损害硅片寿命，但漏电流会随温度指数级增长——结温每升高10°C，漏电流近似翻倍，同时晶体管开关效率下降。为维持时钟频率，GPU需要更高的电压，进而触发动态电压频率调整（DVFS）机制降频，最终导致性能下滑和token产出减少。因此，更优的冷却直接意味着更高的性能和经济效益。

**热阻公式：冷却设计的核心约束**  
Frore的分析基于一个简洁的公式：Tj(max) = T入口 + Q × R总（最大结温 = 冷却液入口温度 + 芯片功耗 × 总热阻）。总热阻由三个主要环节构成：GPU封装本身、封装与冷板之间的导热界面材料（TIM）、冷板设计。每一层热阻都会抬高芯片温度，降低token产出。Nvidia在设计平台时，会为GPU指定最大允许结温（如95°C），而实际运行中，即使未触及该阈值，降低工作温度也能通过减少漏电流来提升效率。

**LiquidJet冷板：半导体工艺的跨界创新**  
传统冷板多采用“刮削”（skiving）工艺制造，在铜块中形成长直微通道。Frore则借鉴半导体制造的蚀刻与键合技术，构建出复杂的三维铜微结构，能够精准针对AI芯片上的热点区域进行冷却。其设计特点包括：围绕热点蚀刻短微通道、多级冷却阶段、以及根据GPU功率密度地图优化的流道布局。根据其分析模型，该技术在Nvidia Rubin GPU上可实现6°C至12°C的结温降低，对应tokens/Watt提升10%至25%，约10°C的降温可带来约15%的token生成效率提升。

**封装层面革新：去盖与导热材料的潜力**  
Frore的白皮书进一步探讨了封装层面的优化空间。其最大胆的预测是：移除Rubin GPU的集成散热器（IHS）和其中的石墨烯TIM，即“去盖”（delidding），可将封装热阻大幅降低，使结温比常规带盖封装低多达20°C，从而提升tokens/Watt多达35%。值得注意的是，已有一些云服务提供商正在探索使用去盖Rubin GPU以提升盈利能力。不过，去盖后芯片的机械可靠性成为重大隐患——裸片在安装和运行中更易因压力不均而开裂，尤其是Rubin采用TSMC CoWoS-L技术连接两颗芯片，互连桥的脆弱性更高。

**导热界面材料的优化对比**  
导热界面材料同样影响显著。据称Nvidia Rubin在带盖封装中默认使用液态金属铟TIM和镀金接触面。而Frore的方案是：去盖封装搭配高性能相变材料（如PTM7950），其整体热阻仍然低于采用液态金属的带盖封装，可带来多达14°C的结温优势和高达28%的tokens/Watt提升。

**设施冷却的经济性变革**  
更高效的冷板不仅影响芯片本身，还改变了数据中心设施冷却的经济模型。Nvidia Rubin设计支持最高45°C的冷却液入口温度，使许多AI数据中心能完全依赖“免费”的室外冷源，无需机械制冷机。虽然进一步降低入口温度能提升GPU效率，但必须权衡制冷机能耗与token收益。Frore的LiquidJet冷板因在相同结温下需要更低的冷却液流量，降低了机械制冷变得划算所需的制冷机能效比（COP）盈亏平衡点。具体而言，传统冷板需要COP约6.7才能从更冷冷却液中获利，而LiquidJet将这一阈值降至约4.1，使机械制冷在多种部署场景下更具经济吸引力。

**技术对比与适用范围**  
Frore的分析还指出，由于Rubin数据中心的晶体管密度高于Blackwell，LiquidJet冷板在Rubin上的效率提升更为显著。

**总结与重要提示**  
Frore白皮书的核心观点是：冷却已成为AI数据中心盈利能力的决定性变量——降低GPU结温不只是防止过热，而是直接提升token生成效率。基于分析热模型（非实验数据），该公司声称其LiquidJet冷板可降低结温6-12°C、提升tokens/Watt 10-25%；更高效的冷板可使机械制冷在更广泛的数据中心中具备经济性；而去盖封装和优化TIM可进一步降低热阻、提升tokens/Watt达35%，但伴随机械可靠性风险。需要强调的是，这些结论均基于Frore自己的分析模型，实际效果有待真实环境验证。

history.content: Driven by demand for AI capacity, AMD’s data center revenue more than doubled year-over-year in its latest earnings report, reaching $6.7 billion. That’s up from $5.8 billion in Q1, and jumping 107 percent from the $3.2 billion it reported for the same period a year ago. During Tuesday’s earnings call, AMD CEO Lisa Su said the company expects “data center segment revenue to more than double year-over-year in 2027,” as well.At the same time, AMD’s gaming revenue fell 31 percent compared to last year, to $779 million, as price hikes and component shortages slowed sales for the Xbox Series X / S, PS5, and Valve’s Steam Deck. On a call after the earnings were released, Su told analysts that, “Gaming graphics revenue also declined year-over-year, as higher industry-wide component costs contributed to higher graphics card prices and weighed on overall demand.”Image: AMD“Revenue increased 50 percent year-over-year to a record $11.5 billion, driven by continued strength in our Data Center business, which represented 58% of company revenue in the quarter,” wrote AMD CFO Jean Hu. Its overall PC and gaming business revenue grew six percent compared to last year, with Client revenue up 23 percent thanks to Ryzen processor sales.“AI is driving a significant expansion in demand for compute across all of our markets, and our leadership portfolio and growing customer visibility position us exceptionally well to capture this expanding opportunity and deliver substantial revenue and earnings growth in the years ahead,” said AMD CEO Lisa Su.Update, August 4th: Added comments from AMD’s earnings call.

history.titleZh: AMD数据中心业务蓬勃发展，游戏业务退居其次
history.descriptionZh:
AMD最新季度财报显示，在AI算力需求爆发的强力驱动下，其数据中心业务表现极为亮眼：该部门营收达到67亿美元，较上季度的58亿美元环比增长，更同比暴增107%（去年同期为32亿美元）。这一数字意味着数据中心已经取代传统PC成为AMD的绝对增长引擎，当季占公司总营收的58%。AMD CEO苏姿丰在财报电话会上进一步表示，预计2027年数据中心部门营收仍将保持同比翻倍以上的增长势头，彰显出市场对AI加速芯片持续且旺盛的渴求。

与此形成鲜明对比的是，AMD的游戏业务遭遇明显滑铁卢，季度营收降至7.79亿美元，同比下降31%。苏姿丰将下滑归因于行业性组件成本上涨推高了显卡价格，从而抑制了消费需求；Xbox Series X/S、PS5以及Steam Deck等游戏主机的销售也因价格因素和元器件短缺而承压。这凸显出AI算力对芯片产能的挤占正在深刻重塑半导体行业的供需格局，游戏显卡优先级被迫后移。

从整体财务数据看，AMD当季总营收创下115亿美元的历史纪录，同比增长50%。CFO Jean Hu在报告中强调，增长主要源于数据中心的持续强力表现。分业务来看，客户端（PC）业务营收同比增长23%，得益于锐龙（Ryzen）处理器出货强劲；PC和游戏业务合计营收同比增长6%，但增长贡献明显由PC端拉动。

在技术层面，AMD目前正通过Instinct系列加速器（如MI300系列）与EPYC服务器处理器双线并进，争夺NVIDIA在AI训练和推理市场的份额。其创新点在于将CPU与GPU（以及HBM高带宽内存）通过Chiplet架构和统一内存池进行异构集成，有效降低数据搬运开销、提升能效比，并借助开放软件生态（ROCm）为用户提供更灵活的AI基础设施选择。苏姿丰强调，“AI正推动所有市场对计算需求的显著扩展”，AMD凭借领先的产品组合和不断增长的客户可见度，有望在未来的算力浪潮中持续实现营收与利润的高速增长。

此次财报背后折射出的行业趋势值得关注：一方面，AI数据中心建设仍处于超级周期，头部云厂商和企业的资本开支持续向加速计算倾斜；另一方面，消费级游戏市场则因芯片产能分流和终端价格上涨而阶段性承压。AMD的战略重心正在全面转向AI基础设施，这一转型既反映了市场结构的深刻变化，也为其在2027年“数据中心营收再翻倍”的远期目标奠定了路径基础。随着更多AI推理负载下沉到企业端和边缘侧，AMD凭借相对开放的生态和更具竞争力的性价比，有望在NVIDIA主导的AI芯片市场中分得更大的蛋糕。
